articles.title: WNBA Finals: Atlanta Dream beat Golden State Valkyries to force decider
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream win Game 6 against Golden State Valkyries to keep series alive and send WNBA Finals to deciding game this weekend; watch Game 7 of the WNBA Finals from Golden State at 1am on Sunday live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Allisha Gray posted 23 points while Rhyne Howard had 21 as the Dream recovered from back-to-back defeats in Games 4 and 5.

Angel Reese chipped in with a 15-point, 13-rebound double-double for Atlanta, who welcomed a near full-capacity crowd for what had been a 12.30pm tip-off local time.

"You could definitely tell we got our swagger back. First, shout out to the crowd. Being able to come here 12.30pm on a Thursday and so many things going on in the world from school to work, to everything else, we're just super thankful," said Reese.

"We fed off their energy, they were loud from the beginning so we're definitely thankful for that. We wanted to make sure we maximised this opportunity. They just want to go home right now.

"Everybody left everything they had out there and that what was important to us. We knew shots were going to fall, we knew it was coming, we'd put so much work in. I'm just really proud of our team for responding the way we did."

The Dream led by as many as 25 points at one stage before Golden State fought back to pull within 77-66 with two minutes remaining. Gabby Williams led the way for the Valkyries with 26 points, along with 15 in support from Tiffany Hayes.

Atlanta led 46-26 at half-time having asserted their dominance with a 13-0 run and seen their opponents manage just nine of 34 from the field in the opening two quarters.

"They scored 32 points in the first quarter, that's unacceptable on our end," said Golden State guard Veronica Burton.

"Just got to play better defense. They were hitting good shots and getting good looks. We were spread out a little bit. We cleaned it up in other quarters defensively, but we can't let that happen. There needs to be a sense of urgency, it's the WNBA finals."

Game 7 takes place in Golden State from 1am on Sunday, live on Sky Sports .

articles.title: Fixer Pleads Guilty to Bribery and Wire Fraud Charges in NCAA Basketball Point-Shaving Scheme
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — An Arkansas man has pleaded guilty to charges of bribery and wire fraud for his role in a point-shaving scheme involving NCAA Division I basketball games.
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — An Arkansas man has pleaded guilty to charges of bribery and wire fraud for his role in a point-shaving scheme involving NCAA Division I basketball games.

Rodrick Winkler, 32, pleaded guilty in U.S. District Court on Monday to bribery in sporting contests, conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud charges for scheming to influence games from September 2022 to February 2025.

The guilty plea stems from a January indictment that ensnared 26 people, including more than a dozen college basketball players who tried to fix games.

Winkler was a "fixer" in the scheme to recruit and bribe college basketball players to underperform and help ensure their team failed to cover the spread, according to court filings. The scheme involved 39 players over 17 different teams who fixed or attempted to fix 29 NCAA games.

The scheme resulted in more than $3 million in fraudulent wagers placed on the games and more than $1.1 million in financial losses to sportsbooks throughout the country, according to the court. Winkler and other fixers offered the players bribe payments usually ranging from $10,000 to $30,000 per game.

The schemers also profited from fixing Chinese Basketball Association games before turning to NCAA games.

Winkler is scheduled to be sentenced on Feb. 8 and faces a maximum possible term of 45 year in prison, three years of supervised release and a fine.

articles.title: Rudy Gobert Responds to Viral Video of LaMelo Ball's Apparent Frustration on T-Wolves Bench
articles.summary: Rudy Gobert isn't worried about an interaction with LaMelo Ball that turned some heads during Wednesday's loss to the Golden State Warriors.
articles.body:
Rudy Gobert isn't worried about an interaction with LaMelo Ball that turned some heads during Wednesday's loss to the Golden State Warriors.

"I'd like to see the images, see what it looks like," Gobert said Thursday, per Jon Krawczynski of The Athletic. "In the moment I didn't feel like it was anything bad. And there's been bad things in the past. But that wasn't anything bad."

He was referring to a video of Ball appearing to show frustration toward the big man on the bench during the 119-114 loss.

"Sometimes people make an assumption and it's totally something different, with the angles and stuff," Gobert continued. "There might be some of that. But I didn't feel any animosity. There was some frustration, for sure. I was frustrated. They were frustrated. Those guys have been great."

It was a game to forget for Gobert, who finished with one point and four rebounds in 20 minutes of action. He missed all four of his field-goal attempts and was largely a nonfactor in the close loss.

On the other side, Stephen Curry erupted for 44 points, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg added 26 points in support. It was Golden State's second straight win after it lost three consecutive games to start the 2026-27 campaign.

It has been largely the opposite for Minnesota, which started 3-0 but has now lost two in a row.

More concerning than the small losing streak is Anthony Edwards' knee injury , which is expected to sideline him for the foreseeable future. Edwards is Minnesota's go-to offensive option and someone who would be relied on to keep pace with fellow stars like Curry in games like Wednesday's.

His absence puts more of the onus on players such as Ball and Gobert to contribute and keep the Timberwolves in the middle of the Western Conference playoff picture.

They were unable to keep pace with Curry and Co. on Wednesday, and additional frustration may build if the losses continue. For now, though, Gobert isn't concerned about his latest interaction with Ball.

articles.title: 76ers' Jaylen Brown Says 'Just Not Giving a F--k' Allows Him to Deal with Outside Noise
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown explained how he manages outside noise without letting it affect him.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Jaylen Brown explained how he manages outside noise without letting it affect him.

"I think in some ways I do," Brown said on Thursday's episode of The Old Man and the Three (42:48 mark). "Especially when it comes to character assassination or defamation, things like that where people insinuate things about you that are not true. Then you'll really get me going. But outside of that, people's opinions or whatever the case may be, it's just the art form of not giving a f--k. You can practice it, you can work on it, you can develop it and get better at it."

"They move the bar constantly," he added. "You're chasing the bar that doesn't exist. Like, who is the best player in the world? Or, who is the MVP this year? All these different type of things, it's subjective. The media, there's the people that you need to vote for you to win these awards, sometimes they vote for their favorites or they vote for the storyline they want to win. It's marketing, it moves. If I'm chasing what moves, I'm never gonna be content. I'm never gonna be happy. So, I could care less what they think about me."

Brown is beginning his first season as a member of the 76ers after they acquired him in a blockbuster trade with the Boston Celtics on July 1.

The five-time All-Star departed the Celtics after spending the first 10 years of his career with them, as rumors have surrounded his exit from the organization as well as his relationship with former teammate Jayson Tatum.

Brown has helped Philadelphia open its 2026-27 campaign with a 4-1 record as the team looks to contend in the Eastern Conference.

He's averaging 20.6 points, 6.6 rebounds, 4.2 assists and 1.2 steals per game while shooting 44.2 percent from the field and 40.9 percent from three-point territory.

articles.title: Ben Simmons Says He's a 'Unicorn,' Vows to Return After Achilles Injury Derailed NBA Comeback
articles.summary: Ben Simmons will miss his second straight NBA season after he suffered a torn Achilles before ever taking the court for the Sacramento Kings in a regular-season game, but there is no shortage of self-confidence when it comes to his eventual return.
articles.body:
Ben Simmons will miss his second straight NBA season after he suffered a torn Achilles before ever taking the court for the Sacramento Kings in a regular-season game, but there is no shortage of self-confidence when it comes to his eventual return.

"I'm more than capable of playing in this league," Simmons said, per Marc J. Spears of Andscape. "I'm built for this. I'm not a normal guy. I'm kind of like a unicorn in the sense of how I play the game. I'm not your typical player. I don't know how to put it, but I feel like I'm a lot different than most."

When he first entered the NBA as the No. 1 overall pick of the 2016 NBA draft, there was no doubting his "unicorn" status.

He is the size of a frontcourt player at 6'10" but brought a combination of skills to the league that included the ball-handling and facilitating of a point guard, the ability to get out in transition like a speedy wing, and the defensive versatility to defend across the positional spectrum.

Simmons' resume during his first four seasons on the court for the Philadelphia 76ers included a Rookie of the Year, two All-Defensive First-Team selections, three All-Star nods and a spot on the 2019-20 All-NBA Third-Team.

Philadelphia seemed to have a foundational cornerstone to build around, but questions about his offensive game and lack of aggression when it came to shooting became an issue during the team's 2021 second-round loss to the Atlanta Hawks.

He then missed the entire 2021-22 season and was not the same player for the Brooklyn Nets and Los Angeles Clippers.

The LSU product sat out the 2025-26 campaign but was set for a return to the Kings this season until he suffered the injury.

"My mentality is that I'll be back," Simmons said. "I'll do everything in my power to get back, get healthy and be better than I was before. There is nothing but time and opportunity to do so. So, I'm going to attack it the way I am now."

articles.title: 5-Star Reese Alston, Son of 'Skip to My Lou' Rafer, Makes CBB Commitment Between Kentucky, LSU, More
articles.summary: Top point guard prospect Reese Alston committed to LSU, he announced alongside his family on Thursday.
articles.body:
Top point guard prospect Reese Alston committed to LSU, he announced alongside his family on Thursday.

Alston is a 5-star prospect who's listed as the No. 3 point guard and No. 9 overall player in the 2027 recruiting class, per 247Sports' composite rankings .

He chose to join LSU and head coach Will Wade over finalists including Kentucky, Louisville, Tennessee and Wichita State.

"The internet makes coach Wade out to be somebody he's not," Alston told ESPN's Paul Biancardi (h/t ESPN's Jeff Borzello ). "He has kept his word and showed up ... He's made me a priority."

Alston also received offers from schools including Purdue, Kansas, Houston, Florida State, Texas and USC.

He ultimately chose to join the Tigers after visiting their campus on Sept. 3.

"When I went on campus and saw how I fit and the environment, that really stuck out to me," Alston said, per 247Sports' Brandon Jenkins . "Everyone has questions about coach Wade, but I feel what he showed me over the summer through trusting in me and displaying qualities he possesses as a head coach was very crucial to me."

Alston is the son of former NBA guard Rafer Alston, who suited up for six teams across his 11 seasons in the association.

The younger Alston currently plays in high school for Houston Second Baptist and is coming off an impressive 2025-26 season in which he helped lead his team to its second straight TAPPS 5A State Championship. He averaged 22.2 points, 3.9 rebounds, 5.3 assists and 2.7 steals per game.

Alston is the third member of LSU's 2027 recruiting class , joining 4-star combo guard King Gibson and 4-star power forward Ahmad Hudson.

For the 2026-27 season, the Tigers are looking to return to the NCAA tournament as Wade begins his second stint as head coach after failing to make a March Madness appearance in each of the prior four years.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards Holds Auditions for Body Double in Funny New Adidas Video After Injury
articles.summary: The third episode of Adidas' sketch-comedy web series Minnatlantasota featuring Minnesota Timberwolves superstar Anthony Edwards dropped on Thursday.
articles.body:
The third episode of Adidas' sketch-comedy web series Minnatlantasota featuring Minnesota Timberwolves superstar Anthony Edwards dropped on Thursday.

The episode features Edwards looking for a body double in case he had to miss time with injury and potentially fall short of the 65-game minimum needed to be eligible for major end-of-season awards.

Unfortunately, Edwards will miss time after undergoing a successful right knee arthroscopic procedure for debridement. Thankfully, the Wolves announced he is expected to recover fully.

Minnesota has not announced a timetable for his return, but ESPN's Shams Charania reported Tuesday that Edwards may miss up to two months.

When the video was filmed, exactly, is unclear but it almost certainly wasn't anytime after the injury.

Edwards started the year on fire, averaging nearly a point-per-minute (33.3 points in 33.8 minutes per game) over the Timberwolves' first four contests. Minnesota won its first three games by a combined 70 points before dropping a pair of close ones to fall to 3-2.

articles.title: Ohio Supreme Court Keeps Two Dozen Basketball Players Eligible with Season Openers Looming
articles.summary: COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — The Ohio Supreme Court filed an order Thursday that will keep the two dozen players involved in an eligibility case in that state available to play for teams across the country, with the start of college basketball season beginning next week.
articles.body:
COLUMBUS, Ohio (AP) — The Ohio Supreme Court filed an order Thursday that will keep the two dozen players involved in an eligibility case in that state available to play for teams across the country, with the start of college basketball season beginning next week.

The order kept in place a ruling from earlier this month, when the state's high court stayed a lower-court ruling that would have declared the players ineligible.

The NCAA is the defendant in a case filed by lead plaintiff Filip Borovicanin of Xavier, which opens its season on Monday. Other basketball players in the case include Gonzaga's Javon Bennett, Cincinnati's MJ Collins and Auburn's Kolby King.

The court became involved in the college eligibility issue when it was asked to determine the legality of an executive order issued earlier this month by Gov. Mike DeWine that granted athletes in Ohio who graduated from high school in 2022 a fifth year of college eligibility in defiance of NCAA rules.

Part of the case involved both parties asking the court to weigh in on the Borovicanin case.

The NCAA then sued DeWine in federal court, saying his order made it "impossible for all schools to compete on a level playing field."

Earlier this year, the NCAA passed a rule granting players five seasons of eligibility, but it did not include the high school class of '22 in the new rule. That, in turn, has triggered dozens of lawsuits across the country and created chaos as coaches try to finalize their rosters.

articles.title: LSU Coach Will Wade Declines to Discuss RJ Luis Jr.'s Status with the Tigers
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU coach Will Wade declined on Thursday to take questions about RJ Luis Jr., who a day earlier won a temporary restraining order that could open a door for him to play for the Tigers — if Wade adds him to his roster.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — LSU coach Will Wade declined on Thursday to take questions about RJ Luis Jr., who a day earlier won a temporary restraining order that could open a door for him to play for the Tigers — if Wade adds him to his roster.

"I'd like to talk about some eligibility stuff, but I'm not talking about that. I can't talk about that," Wade said before taking any questions about his team, which opens the regular season on Tuesday night against LSU-New Orleans.

"I've made my stance very clear on things," Wade added, "and my stance has not changed."

Wade has previously stated that he intended to follow "SEC protocols" regarding Luis, but the latest court order in the case ostensibly bans Wade from doing that.

The NCAA has argued that Luis is not eligible to play because he left college to participate in the NBA draft and not only failed to withdraw as required to return to college, but briefly spent time with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics during the 2025 offseason and preseason.

The Southeastern Conference also has ruled Luis ineligible, saying its own rules ban players who have participated in the NBA, WBNA or NFL drafts, or signed contracts with teams from those leagues.

Luis' lawyers — Elliot Abrams and Tony Clayton — have asserted that their client, who never played in an NBA game, is no more of a pro than numerous players from overseas who played for developmental professional teams before being granted waivers by the NCAA to play in college in the U.S.

In late August, a Louisiana judge issued a preliminary injunction against the NCAA that effectively made Luis eligible to play in college pending the resolution of his case. On Wednesday, that ruling by state District Judge Ronald R. Johnson in East Baton Rouge Parish was expanded to include the Southeastern Conference and LSU.

Specifically, the latest ruling temporarily bars the SEC from punishing LSU if it plays Luis. It also forbids LSU from citing SEC rules as a reason for declining to play Luis.

The ruling puts Wade, who recruited Luis, in the awkward position of having to choose between defying the SEC or the court — unless he can come up with some other reason why Luis is no longer welcome on the team.

Clayton said Thursday that if LSU does not place Luis on the roster, he intends to keep up the legal push for his client's right to play.

The newest injunction takes effect before LSU's season opener and lasts until a hearing — tentatively set for Nov. 13 — can be held in the case.

The SEC has a long-established rule forbidding teams from adding players with major professional experience to their rosters. In September, the conference announced updated enforcement provisions to that rule, stating that the commissioner had the power to suspend coaches, fine universities up to half of a sport's budget and restrict a member university's voting privileges on conference matters.

Under threat of being voted out of the SEC by fellow league members, LSU elected in early September not to add to its football roster two players who'd spent part of the offseason with NFL clubs before being recruited back to college by Tigers first-year coach Lane Kiffin.

Those players, Dae'Quan Wright and Zxavian Harris, had played for Kiffin at Mississippi. During Week 1 of the season, they were granted a preliminary injunction against the NCAA and SEC by another state judge in Baton Rouge.

That case led the SEC to file a federal case alleging that LSU, by attempting to circumvent SEC rules, was violating the league's First Amendment right of expressive association. In other words, the SEC essentially argued it has the right to enforce rules governing competition among members who all chose to join the league.

Luis, the 2025 Big East Player of the Year with St. John's, played three seasons of college basketball with two teams before declaring for the 2025 NBA draft.

articles.title: Dream beat Valkyries 80-69 to force Game 7 of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Allisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard had 21 as the hot-shooting Atlanta Dream held off Golden State’s late rally to take an 80-69 victory over the Valkyries in Game 6 on Thursday and pull even in the WNBA Finals.
articles.body: The Atlanta Dream’s shooters finally found some daylight. And as a result, the Dream’s goal of winning their first WNBA championship is still shining bright. Allisha Gray scored 23 points and Rhyne Howard had 21 as the hot-shooting Dream held off Golden State’s late rally to take an 80-69 victory over the Valkyries in Game 6 on Thursday and pull even in the WNBA Finals. The decisive Game 7 will be played at Golden State on Saturday night as each team seeks its first WNBA championship. After having their lowest scoring games of the Finals in losses in Games 4 and 5, the Dream enjoyed an offensive awakening when faced with the must-win mandate. “It’s been frustrating for all of us not being able to shoot great ... and open shots that we have been getting, not hitting them at the right time,” said Atlanta’s Angel Reese, who recorded a double-double with 15 points and 13 rebounds. “And I always told the girls it’s not going to rain forever. And we were able to maximize that moment today. The sun peaked out a little bit more today and gave us an opportunity to see Game 7.” The Valkyries defense was dominant in a 67-62 Game 4 win and a 64-55 win in Game 5. That left Golden State with a 3-2 series lead and an opportunity to clinch the championship on Thursday. Instead, the Dream claimed the defensive advantage and took commanding leads of 32-15 after the first quarter and 46-26 at halftime. “The way we started in the first quarter was unacceptable on our end,” Golden State guard Veronica Burton said. “You can’t let that happen out of the gate.” After being held to 22 points in the first half of their Game 5 loss, the Dream matched that total in the first 6:30 of the opening quarter. “We knew they were going to be desperate,” Valkyries coach Natalie Nakase said of the Dream. “For us not to match that is disappointing and frustrating. “This is the Finals. The physicality is supposed to be up. You want to have that physicality. You want to have that fight. You want to have that give-it-all mentality. We just did not do that.” On Wednesday, the Dream announced a sellout for Game 6 despite the much-criticized 12:30 p.m. EDT tipoff. There were only scattered empty seats in the upper level despite concerns about work and school obligations hurting the turnout. Gabby Williams led the Valkyries with 26 points. Tiffany Hayes added 15. Atlanta’s biggest lead was 25 points. The Valkyries stormed back in the final minutes, pulling to 77-66 on Laeticia Amihere’s two free throws with 1:57 remaining. A late 3-pointer by Gray cut off the comeback attempt. Gray made 5 of 7 3s. Howard made 4 of 6 from beyond the arc. Much of the production came on 3s. Atlanta made 6 of 8 3s and 11 of 15 shots overall while racing to a 32-15 lead in the first quarter. Dream coach Karl Smesko said his team reclaimed its proper pace on offense. “We played with a different spacing and pace,” Smesko said. “Like, in truth, it’s how we are supposed to play. So it is just getting back to, like, our fundamentals of how we like to play offense. And in the first half, you saw it be catching it ready to shoot.” After leading 6-5, the Dream pulled away with 13 unanswered points in a run that included two 3s from Jordin Canada. Reese joined the 3-point party with a shot from the corner in the second period. The Dream improve to 16-0 when Reese has at least one 3. While Atlanta’s sharp shooting continued for a 46-26 halftime lead, the Valkyries struggled. Golden State made only 9 of 34 shots in the half, often struggling to create open opportunities because of the Dream’s smothering defense. Howard opened the second half with another 3-pointer. Burton was called for a flagrant foul midway through the third period when an officials’ review determined she made an unnecessary windup and contact on Howard’s face as Howard was driving for a basket. Kaila Charles closed the third quarter with a 3-pointer for Golden State that trimmed Atlanta’s lead to 16 points at 63-47. It was the smallest lead for the Dream since the 13-0 run in the opening period. Golden State pulled to within 13 points at 68-55 before Gray and Reese sank 3s to push the lead to 74-55. Williams’ three-point play cut the led to 77-69 before Gray sank a crucial 3-pointer for Atlanta. Hayes was called for her fifth foul in a collision for a loose ball with 5:01 remaining. Hayes left the court slowly after receiving attention from a trainer.

articles.title: Ni la mejor defensa de la Euroliga detiene al Real Madrid
articles.standfirst: Décima victoria seguida de los blancos, que también destrozan al Fenerbahce al ritmo de Maledon (26 puntos y 35 de valoración) y Campazzo (10 puntos y 10 asistencias)
articles.summary: Décima victoria seguida de los blancos, que también destrozan al Fenerbahce al ritmo de Maledon (26 puntos y 35 de valoración) y Campazzo (10 puntos y 10 asistencias)
articles.body: La mejor defensa de la Euroliga tampoco pudo detener a un Real Madrid que sigue lanzado. Son ya 10 victorias consecutivas de los blancos, seis de ellas en la competición europea, donde continúan subiendo como la espuma. Esta vez destrozaron al Fenerbahce, todo un candidato a la Final Four, sin necesidad de otro recital triplista (11/32) y sin meter 100 puntos, lo cual, vista su trayectoria, ya es noticia. Se quedó en 95, que son 23 más de los que encajaban los turcos. Ganó el Madrid al ritmo una vez más de un Maledon imparable. Recuperó su tacto cerca del aro y mantuvo la puntería que ha construido en las últimas fechas. Acabó con 26 puntos (3/4 en triples), siete rebotes, nueve faltas recibidas y 35 de valoración. A este nivel, aspirante al MVP de la Euroliga. Le secundó un gran Campazzo, que dirigió algunos de los mejores momentos del Madrid: 10 puntos, 10 asistencias y 25 de valoración. Y entre pequeños, siempre Tavares: 14 puntos con un solo fallo en el tiro. En un partido con varios sustos de Maledon y Feliz, la peor parte se la llevó Jantunen, que se tuvo que retirar en el segundo cuarto después de una jugada en la que no hubo torcedura ni golpe. “Parece un poquito grave”, dijo Pedro Martínez a la conclusión. Tiene afectada la fascia plantar. Lesión complicada. El Madrid empezó atascado ante la eficaz defensa de cambios planteada por Jasikevicius. Se acumulaban las pérdidas (ocho en el primer cuarto), Feliz se llevó una temprana técnica por protestar y Larkin y Balwin castigaban (4-11). Pero la salida de Campazzo lo cambió todo. Por ritmo y por acierto. Con ocho puntos casi seguidos, incluidos dos triples, el Madrid se puso arriba por primera vez (14-13). El rebote ofensivo y Horton-Tucker (16 puntos al descanso y en blanco después) hacían de contrapeso para llegar a la primera pausa con 22-24 después de un susto de Maledon, al que se le fue la rodilla derecha. Nada importante, como se vio en el segundo periodo. El francés dominó el partido y torturó a su rival a base de penetraciones y faltas forzadas. Lideró un parcial de 19-2 que disparó al Madrid 13 puntos arriba (39-26). La defensa blanca era excelente y el Fenerbahce, que se perdía entre faltas de ataque, sumó una canasta en juego en seis minutos. Después encontró salvavidas en Key, Horton-Tucker y el rebote de ataque, que seguía siendo una sangría para los blancos. Nueve cedieron al descanso. Al menos habían controlado las pérdidas. Los turcos recortaron a cinco al intermedio (47-42). La segunda parte arrancó con un ritmo más bajo. El Fenerbahce llevaba el partido a su terreno, al de pocas posesiones. Después, se desataron los madridistas, que siempre encuentran un momento para sacar de rueda a su rival. Suele ser a golpe de triple. Tras estar mucho mejor cerca del aro que desde el arco, llovieron cuatro casi seguidos de Procida y Okeke, que junto a Jones cumplieron como secundarios, y también de Feliz y Abalde. Campazzo dirigía y ellos ejecutaban. La defensa volvía a ser de mucho nivel. Un parcial de 17-4 llevó la renta a 18 (68-50). Clyburn, único referente otomano en la segunda parte (21 puntos), lo intentó, pero el Fenerbahce no puso aprovechar ni sus 20 rebotes de ataque. El último aliento se lo dejó con un 0-9 (72-64). Feliz tuvo ahí sus mejores minutos, Maledon acertó con un triple, Okeke sentenció (89-71 a falta de 2:36) y el galo se ensañó con otro acierto sobre la bocina para fijar la máxima de toda la noche (95-76). Jugando hasta el último segundo. El Madrid nunca frena. 95 - Real Madrid (22+25+23+25): Maledon (26), Feliz (8), Procida (5), Jantunen (-) y Tavares (14) -cinco inicial-, Luwawu-Cabarrot (8), Pradilla (4), Abalde (8), Campazzo (10), Okeke (6), Llull (-) y Jones (6). 76 - Fenerbahce (24+18+13+21): Larkin (7), Baldwin IV (7), Shields (8), Key (6) y Sanli (-) -cinco titular-, Larkin (-), Bingham (3) Forrest (6), Melli (2), Horton-Tucker (16), Clyburn (21), Silva (-) y Sargiunas (-). articles.title: 'We got our swagger back:' Dream force WNBA Finals Game 7 in rout, but can they maintain shooting rhythm?
articles.summary: Angel Reese was feeling the vibe after Atlanta's stunning early shooting display from 3 in a series that had been more of a rock fight.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — The thing Angel Reese learned in her first WNBA Finals appearance is that long series still go by fast. What's done is done, and what's to come is for the taking.

Trailing 3-2 in the series, and potentially 40 minutes from the experience ending, she and her Atlanta Dream teammates gathered together ahead of film sessions to talk through what it meant. They needed to gain confidence back following two losses marred by offensive woes. They emphasized how each could take a superstar turn, but everyone was needed.

By the end of the day's film and a final practice ahead of a must-win Game 6, they said they felt good about returning to Atlanta Dream basketball. They proved the talk true immediately.

"You could definitely tell we got our swagger back," Reese said.

The Dream's offense tore out of its funk and past the Golden State Valkyries' suffocating defense in Game 6 on Thursday, a jolt to West Coasters settling in with their breakfast for a 12:30 p.m. ET/9:30 a.m. PT tip-off. The 80-69 win was more dominant than the final score indicated; the Dream led by 25 points with three minutes to go until the half.

It forced the first Game 7 in league history, and the Bay Area is preparing for the Halloween contest to be "Boohalla," a play on their home crowd moniker of "Ballhalla."

Atlanta's 32 first-quarter points were the most by either team in any quarter of this Finals and were at least half of its total output in each of its three series losses. The 32-15 advantage was the largest of any first quarter in Finals history.

Valkyries forward Gabby Williams called it "unacceptable" by Golden State, with a lack of ball pressure and aggression the biggest early downfalls.

"They did a good job today of setting the tone early," she said. "Obviously, we didn't."

The Dream won each of their three games by double digits, while the Valkyries' defense kept Atlanta to season lows in each of the Dream's single-digit losses.

"When we can punch first, we've won every single game," Reese said.

Everything after that initial jab was merely dressing, a continuation of the postseason party the Dream held at State Farm Arena. The 17,099 in a sold-out crowd barely registered the Valkyries' late comeback attempts until there was nothing to do but notice. Golden State fought back to within 11 with 2:36 to play — a dangerous spot for the Dream against a squad accustomed to late comebacks. They trailed again by 11 at 1:56, only to miss three 3-point attempts off a steal and two offensive rebounds.

Still, Golden State cut into the lead to pull to within eight, and finally the Dream closed the threat. Reese penetrated to draw a defender and kicked it out to Allisha Gray in the corner. Gray drained it with a screen from DeWanna Bonner to secure an extension of their season for another 40 minutes.

The Dream didn't need Reese to provide the elite offensive play of their previous victories. She missed finishes at the rim (5 of 18) and turned it over six times for a second time in this Finals. But with 15 points and 14 rebounds, she now has four double-doubles in six games.

"It was just a mental mindset of me being able to go out there and try to lead the team as best as I can, no matter how ugly it could be," Reese said. "As long as we came out with the win, I just wanted to do whatever it took."

A 3-pointer by Reese in the second quarter made victory nearly inevitable. The Dream are 16-0 when she makes one, and it was an area she came into the game wanting to maximize. Early in Game 5 she passed up an open look from 3, bypassing the team-wide green light coach Karl Smesko reiterated on Wednesday that includes Reese.

She took them this time, missing two early before hitting net in the second quarter to go up 42-19. By the time she hit her second, the Dream led 74-55 with 5:43 to play as fans began clearing their Halloween schedules. She bounced her way backward down the court before it even went in, a rather subdued Reese reaction for which the crowd more than made up.

The whole team hit fire from deep, a refreshing accomplishment in a defensive slog of a series. They were 6 of 8 in the first quarter from 3, with four of five starters making at least one. Rhyne Howard and Gray, playing with the pinky and ring finger of her shooting hand taped following minor surgery, each went 2 for 2.

By game's end they were 13 of 30 (43.3%) and equally as good from inside the arc (14 of 32, 43%). It is only the second time a team eclipsed the 40% mark in the series. The other was Atlanta in a Game 3 win (49.3%). In an evenly played game elsewhere — neither pulled away that thoroughly in turnovers or points off them — the 3-pointers were the difference.

"It's been frustrating for all of us not being able to shoot great," Reese said. "I always told the girls, 'It's not gonna rain forever,' and we were able to maximize that moment today. And the sun peeked out a little bit more today and gave us the opportunity to see Game 7."

As much confidence as the reemergence instilled in the better offensive squad, the Dream have been here before. They were 40.9% from 3 in the Game 3 win and 49.3% overall, allowing Valkyries head coach Natalie Nakase her favorite thing: bad defensive game film to study and reassess. Atlanta shot worse than 34% in each of its losses and a combined 14 of 74 from 3.

And the Valkyries won the second half, 43-35, by playing their own slower pace to nearly burst the city's dream bubble. Williams led all scorers with 26 points despite another inefficient day (8 of 22) and found her way to the line (7 of 8). It was the first time in the series Golden State attempted more free throws. Laeticia Amihere, a lower bench option ever since a promising Game 1 start as a reserve defender for Reese, was a spark in place of Kiah Stokes.

Nakase lamented her messaging again, rhetorically asking those at-large if the communication to her players was foggy. She knew the Dream were going to come out desperate. And they did.

"We just didn't do it," Nakase said of her team's lack of early defensive pressure that ultimately decided the game. "See how frustrating that is? It's frustrating when we just didn't do it."

Point guard Veronica Burton insisted the Valkyries didn't come into Game 6 thinking they had two chances at the 'chip. Yet, it looked that way. As Williams, who lit a fire under the Valkyries to win two in a row for a series lead, answered questions abruptly, Burton made clear their body language at the podium in the face of an unnerving loss and what they actually felt moving into the final game were two different things.

"At the end of the day, we feel good," Burton said. "Yes, we lost. It was a bad game for us. We had a terrible first quarter, but we cleaned it up. We found a way. We didn't quit. Games 2 and 3 were ugly; we quit, we looked bad."

The question is if the Valks can carry that style back across the country one more time. The league's longest season is officially at its finish line. There aren't bound to be many tricks or surprises between teams that know each other this well. And now the franchise's first championship is either's to claim.

articles.title: Sophie Cunningham says she has about 20 stalkers the FBI is keeping tabs on
articles.summary: Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham says she believes the FBI is watching about 20 people who may be stalking her. One man was arrested this summer alleged...
articles.body:
An Indiana man was arrested this summer for allegedly stalking Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham and sending her threatening and explicit messages on social media.

That's some pretty dark stuff, but it's the kind of thing Cunningham says she has had to deal with quite often over the last few years.

During a recent appearance on the podcast " This Past Weekend w/ Theo Von ," the soon-to-be WNBA free agent made the startling revelation that she thinks that there are "20, I think, people kind of that the FBI are watching for me."

The FBI declined to comment for this article.

The topic came up as Cunningham, who just finished her sixth WNBA season, was discussing the league's massive increase in popularity in recent years with the influx of such young stars as Fever teammate Caitlin Clark , Atlanta Dream's Angel Reese and Dallas Wings' Paige Bueckers .

Cunningham has seen her own popularity soar over the last two years as Clark's on-court protector. She also has become a central figure in a national debate over trans athletes in women's sports, after telling ESPN she wanted to "protect young girls in a locker room, or young girls in sport who shouldn't have to go against biological men."

"The more you're visible on TV, you're going to get more fans," Cunningham told Von. "People are going to know who you are, and that's a really great thing. But there's also a lot of like kind of crazy people, too. Like, we do have a lot of stalkers. I know I do. And that's a negative side of things that people don't think about. And so you do want to feel secure."

One of Cunningham's alleged stalkers is Kevin Singh, 49, who is facing felony charges for stalking and intimidation, as well as a misdemeanor harassment charge. He was arrested June 24 and held in Marion County Jail in Indiana with bail set at $40,000. Last week, a judge denied Singh's request for alteration or revocation of bail. A jury trial is scheduled for January.

According to the arrest affidavit, Singh sent Cunningham numerous messages on X and in September 2025 personally delivered a package marked with her name to the Fever's arena (it contained a letter and a Guns N' Roses T-shirt sprayed with men's cologne).

Cunningham told investigators she had been having nightmares and was staying at home more because of Singh's behavior, the affidavit said.

At least now, she is able to joke (kind of) about it.

"His name's Kevin. And the worst part about that is I have a miniature donkey named Kevin," she told Von. "And now I'm like, well, s—, do I need to rename Kevin?"

Last year, a 55-year-old Texas man was sentenced to 2½ years in prison after pleading guilty to stalking and harassing Clark.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.summary: Gana con claridad al Vilnius al que le endosa su primera derrota para liderar el grupo A
articles.body: El Casademont Zaragoza parece abonado a la rutina de convertir las noches europeas en grandes victorias y así lo volvió a demostrar ante el Kibirkstis-Toks lituano en el pabellón Príncipe Felipe (77-55). Era un duelo de invictos, pero fue el Casademont quien impuso su ley tras un inicio con dudas, pero en el que las jugadoras de Carlos Cantero supieron controlar el juego y aprovecharon el apoyo de un público que se divirtió con su equipo. El encuentro entre los dos mejores conjuntos del grupo A comenzó a un ritmo muy alto y las lituanas se pusieron por delante con dos triples de Niyah Becker y una poderosa Daugile Use en la pintura sacando rédito de las pérdidas de un dubitativo Casademont. Ornella Bankolé, que entró a cancha muy enchufada, fue la encargada de espabilar a las locales, aunque fue Aisha Sheppard quien las puso por delante con dos triples consecutivos (19-17) y consiguieron aguantar la ventaja hasta el final del primer cuarto (25-22). Sheppard, Carla Brito y Kristine Vitola pusieron la marcha directa para el Casademont al inicio del segundo cuarto (34-22) ante un Kibirkstis al que ni los tiempos muertos de su entrenador le hicieron reaccionar. Merritt Hempe empezó a hacerse notar en el partido y, aunque parecía que un intercambio de canastas favorecía a las lituanas, el Príncipe Felipe reconoció con aplausos el trabajo silencioso de Brito, que aumentó la distancia con varias canastas antes del descanso (45-31). El tercer cuarto arrancó con ambos conjuntos muy imprecisos de cara al aro y tuvo que llegar Mariona Ortiz para imponer la calma necesaria, anotar un triple y asistir a otro de Veronika Vorackova para ponerse 21 arriba (54-33). Las jugadoras de Vilnius, totalmente desaparecidas, no supieron por donde les llegaban los golpes de las pupilas de Cantero, que completaron una autentica exhibición y solo dejaron anotar a sus rivales seis puntos en el tercer cuarto (63-37). El orgullo de las lituanas, representado por Becker y Brigita Sinickaite, intentó maquillar el resultado al inicio del último cuarto, ante unas rivales que aprovecharon para rotar y repartir minutos y parecieron algo relajadas (67-45). Aún así, el Casademont fue claro dominador del juego y el Príncipe Felipe se divirtió con las jugadas de las suyas en una nueva noche europea en la que se comprobó el potencial que tienen el equipo aragonés en la competición europea (77-55). 77 - Casademont Zaragoza (25+20+18+14): Nadia Fingall (3), Mariona Ortiz (7), Merritt Hempe (8), Aisha Sheppard (16), Veronika Vorackova (11) -cinco inicial- Bankolé (8), Flores (5), Brito (6), Oma (2) Garzon (8) y Vitola (3). 55 – Kibirkstis-Toks (22+9+6+18): Niyah Becker (17), Brigita Sinickaite (8), Daugile Use (4), Zoe Wadoux (4), Nausia Woolfolk (8) -cinco inicial- Meskonyte (8), Makurat (2), Paliulyte (2) y Miknaite (2) Árbitros: Vlad-Theodor Cotrobas-Dascalu (Rumanía), Jordan Wallet (Francia) y Armin Mutapcic (Alemania). articles.title: Spurs' Victor Wembanyama embraces competitive edge but rejects villain label after NBA playoff lessons
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama tells "60 Minutes" he wasn't bothered by his villain label during the NBA Finals but admits he crossed the line at times.
articles.body: Victor Wembanyama is unquestionably one of basketball's brightest young stars. In his third NBA season, he led the San Antonio Spurs to the Finals. San Antonio ultimately lost the series to the New York Knicks in five games. Wembanyama earned several individual honors, including his first Defensive Player of the Year award and All-NBA selection. The French-born Spurs forward opened the 2026-27 season under enormous expectations. The 7-foot-4 star was a preseason favorite to win the NBA MVP award, while San Antonio entered the season as an odds-on favorite to win the championship. The postseason also marked a notable shift in how the public viewed Wembanyama. Once a widely beloved sports figure, he was increasingly cast by some as a villain. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER A series of on-court incidents fueled claims that Wembanyama had become a "dirty" player. One of those situations surfaced in the Western Conference semifinals, when his elbow made contact with then-Minnesota Timberwolves center Naz Reid. During the Finals, many Knicks fans grew furious at times over Wembanyama’s defense against Jalen Brunson. Once viewed as a conquering hero, Wembanyama was quickly cast as a New York sports villain. But he insisted the criticism does not faze him. "No, it didn't because I'm not paying attention to this ... during the Finals. I don't think any player on either team really is," Wembanyama told "60 Minutes" when asked about his portrayal as a villain in a clip released Thursday ahead of Sunday’s full sit-down interview. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Although Wembanyama said he tunes out much of the noise, he does not appear eager to let the villain label stick. He added that last season’s playoff run taught him where to draw the line between playing with a competitive edge and going a step farther than he should, acknowledging that he crossed it at times. VICTOR WEMBANYAMA ADMITS TO HARSH TRUTHS AFTER COSTLY MISTAKE AT END OF NBA FINALS GAME "It showed my limits more than anything else. Going out there, you need to play basketball. You don't need to beat the s--- out of people. [laughs] If you wanna win, at least," Wembanyama said while reflecting on the lessons he learned from last season’s playoff run. Wembanyama also drew public attention before some Finals games began. He was seen standing with his arms crossed during the U.S. national anthem before Game 1, but reportedly was not on the court for the anthems before Games 3 and 4. He has not publicly explained why he stood with his arms crossed before Game 1 on June 3. Wembanyama has played in all five of San Antonio’s regular-season games this season, averaging 25 points per game. articles.title: Kansas Jayhawks Forward Keanu Dawes On the Watch List
articles.summary: Award Preseason Top 20 Watch List
articles.body:
Kansas Jayhawks forward Keanu Dawes continues to collect preseason recognition ahead of the 2026-27 college basketball season after being named to the Karl Malone Power Forward of the Year Top 20 Preseason Watch List. The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame announced the selection Thursday, Oct. 29, giving the Kansas senior another opportunity to receive national recognition heading into his first season in Lawrence.

Dawes is one of 20 players selected for the preseason watch list, which recognizes some of the top power forwards in Division I men's college basketball. The award is named after NBA Hall of Famer Karl Malone, who enjoyed an outstanding professional career and won two NBA Most Valuable Player awards.

According to the official Kansas Athletics announcement , Dawes joins an impressive group of players from around the country competing for the honor.

The Houston native enters the season as a senior after transferring to Kansas from Utah last summer. During his final season with the Utes, Dawes started all 32 games and averaged 12.5 points and 8.8 rebounds per contest. His rebounding average ranked fourth in the Big 12, demonstrating his ability to make an impact on the glass against quality competition.

Dawes also recorded 11 double-doubles last season, showing his consistency as both a scorer and rebounder. One of his strongest performances came against Kansas on Feb. 7, when he recorded 22 points and 12 rebounds against the Jayhawks.

Now wearing a Kansas uniform, Dawes brings valuable experience to head coach Bill Self's frontcourt. His ability to rebound, score around the basket and contribute defensively gives Kansas another important option as it prepares for a challenging schedule.

The recognition also highlights the expectations surrounding Kansas' frontcourt this season. Dawes will have an opportunity to play alongside experienced players and help establish a physical presence in the paint. His rebounding ability could be particularly important as the Jayhawks compete against some of the strongest frontcourts in the country.

The Karl Malone Award is entering its 13th season. The watch list will be narrowed to 10 players in February before five finalists are selected in March. The winner will be chosen by a committee consisting of college basketball personnel, media members, coaches and Hall of Famers.

Dawes is also one of six Big 12 players represented on the preseason list, highlighting the conference's talent at the power forward position.

For Kansas, having Dawes recognized nationally adds another positive storyline heading into the regular season. The Jayhawks have championship expectations, and his experience could become an important part of their success.

Dawes now has an opportunity to turn the preseason recognition into an award-worthy season while helping Kansas compete for another Big 12 championship.

Kansas opens its regular season against Fordham on Nov. 2 at Allen Fieldhouse. JayhawksRoundtable .

articles.title: NBA Cup 2026: How does it work, schedule, format, bracket, odds, location for NBA's in-season tournament
articles.summary: Here is everything you need to know about the NBA Cup, which tips off on Oct. 30.
articles.body:
Last December, the New York Knicks defeated an overwhelmed-looking young San Antonio Spurs team to win the NBA Cup.

Sound familiar? It foreshadowed what would happen in June, when the Knicks won their first title in 53 years. Now the NBA Cup is back starting Friday night, Oct. 30, so which teams are going to make a run and stake their claim to follow in the Knicks ' footsteps? Here is everything you need to know about the 2026 edition of the NBA Cup.

The format hasn't changed since the NBA Cup launched four years ago. The one big change this season is that the NBA Cup semifinals will take place on a team's home court (the higher East and West seed remaining), and the NBA Cup Final will be played at the Hinkle Fieldhouse in Indianapolis, home to the Butler Bulldogs — and the place where the real-life game the movie "Hoosiers" was based on was played.

All 30 teams have been drawn into one of six groups (five teams in each group, three East groups and three West groups). Each team plays the other teams in its group once — four games total — and those games count double as both regular season games and NBA Cup games.

The six group winners plus a wild card from each conference — determined by head-to-head record and point differential — go into an eight-team knockout round bracket (East vs. East, West vs. West, similar to the NBA playoffs where the conferences are separate until the Finals). The knockout round games are single-elimination.

The Final two teams, one East and one West, will head to Indianapolis for the Dec. 11 championship game.

Thanks to the bright, specially designed courts, fans will instantly recognize these as NBA Cup games when they tune in every Friday starting Oct. 30 and running through Nov. 27 (on Amazon Prime), with Cup games on NBC and Peacock on Nov. 24 (Celtics at Wizards, then Mavericks at Nuggets), as well as on ESPN Nov. 25.

NBA Cup games will be played on specially designed courts with the home team wearing their Statement Edition uniforms.

No one will confuse these with standard regular-season games.

Here's a look at the NBA Cup 2026 groups (with some analysis added at the end).

West Group A: Dallas Mavericks, Denver Nuggets, Houston Rockets, Phoenix Suns, Utah Jazz

West Group B: LA Clippers, Memphis Grizzlies, Minnesota Timberwolves, New Orleans Pelicans, Oklahoma City Thunder

West Group C: Golden State Warriors, Los Angeles Lakers, Portland Trail Blazers, Sacramento Kings, San Antonio Spurs

Analysis: As with much of this early NBA season, injuries are robbing us of some of the joy of these matchups. Specifically in Group B, where the Timberwolves and Thunder would have been a real showdown, but with no Anthony Edwards, Jalen Williams or Cason Wallace, it's not the same. Even with the injuries, OKC is the team to beat in Group B.

Group C has some interesting matchups with the Lakers, Spurs, and fun-to-watch Warriors, but I expect San Antonio will win out in the end. In Group A, Denver will be the favorite, led by Nikola Jokic. Cooper Flagg makes Dallas dangerous. Yet, for my money, the best team in this group is the Houston Rockets, so look for Kevin Durant and company to advance.

East Group A: Brooklyn Nets, Detroit Pistons, Milwaukee Bucks, Orlando Magic, Toronto Raptors

East Group B: Cleveland Cavaliers, Indiana Pacers, Miami Heat, New York Knicks, Philadelphia 76ers

East Group C: Atlanta Hawks, Boston Celtics, Charlotte Hornets, Chicago Bulls, Washington Wizards.

Analysis: Group B is the "Group of Death" (to borrow a soccer term): Cleveland, New York or Philadelphia could take this, and while Miami may not advance, on a given night it can beat anyone behind Giannis Antetokounmpo. If Tyrese Haliburton were healthy, this group would be impossible to predict. As it is, give me the Cavaliers, who are playing well to start the season.

Group A would have been a lot more interesting if Kawhi Leonard were healthy (and maybe he returns in time to impact games), but this group feels like Detroit's to lose. In Group C, Boston is the obvious favorite, but sleep on Atlanta and Washington at your own peril.

What's the schedule for the NBA Cup 2026?

Most NBA Cup games will be played on Friday nights starting on Oct. 30, and running through Nov. 27, with games highlighted on Amazon Prime (which will also broadcast the semifinals and Cup Final). Cup games will air on NBC and Peacock on Nov. 24, and on ESPN on Nov. 25.

The six group winners plus two wild cards (one from each conference) advance to the knockout rounds. Starting with the semifinals, the entire show moves to the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

Here are the odds for the top 10 teams to win the NBA Cup 2024, via our partners at DraftKings:

San Antonio +425 Oklahoma City +550 Boston +700 Philadelphia +1200 Houston +1300 Detroit +1300 New York +1600 Denver +1600 Toronto +2000 Portland +2200

The players get money — and make no mistake, that is the biggest motivation. Players talk openly about it.

There is a trophy, and teams will hang a banner. Even the Knicks. Eventually. For fan bases, winning the NBA Cup can be celebrated as a sign the team is on the right track, like the Knicks a year ago. However, for the players, it's about the money. Each player on the championship team will receive more than half a million dollars. Each player on the NBA Cup runner-up team gets more than $200,000. Players from the two teams that advanced to the semifinals but lost will each receive more than $100,000. Players on teams that advanced out of group play but lost in the quarterfinals will get more than $50,000 each. While even the championship money is comparable to another game check for a star like Giannis Antetokounmpo or Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, it can be a meaningful bump for players on minimum salaries at the end of the bench. The stars realize who they are playing for when things get serious.

The New York Knicks, behind stellar play from NBA Cup MVP Jalen Brunson. As noted, they handed Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs a Cup Final loss that would be echoed next June. In 2024, Milwaukee bounced back from an ugly 2-8 start to the season to find its footing in NBA Cup games and went on a run behind Giannis Antetokounmpo, reaching the Cup Finals against Oklahoma City. Once there, Antetokounmpo had a 26-point triple-double, completely controlling the game on both sides of the ball. LeBron James and the Los Angeles Lakers won the inaugural 2023 NBA In-Season Tournament (before it was officially branded as the NBA Cup).

Where is the NBA Cup 2026 Final being held?

The NBA is moving the NBA Cup Final to Indianapolis's iconic Hinkle Fieldhouse, the home of Butler University.

Famously, Hinkle Fieldhouse hosted the 1954 Indiana high school state championship game that inspired the 1986 movie "Hoosiers," and climactic scenes from the film were shot there.

The NBA Cup is Commissioner Adam Silver's baby.

He pushed for this and got the owners to buy in — and Silver has largely been proven right. The fact that broadcast rights for the NBA Cup were part of the league's massive $7.6 billion new television deal was a huge win for Silver (and means the Cup isn't going anywhere for a long time). At the end of the day, the NBA is a business and adding the Cup brought the league and its players more money.

When first promoting the Cup idea, Silver listed a few reasons he believed it would work for the NBA. First, drawing on the European soccer model, the idea was to create a second trophy of value — clearly not as important as an NBA title, but still meaningful — for teams to compete for and fan bases to cheer. It was something to combat the "championship or bust" mentality of some fans.

Additionally, Silver and the league office have been exploring ways to increase casual fan interest in regular-season games. Silver wants to end, or at least diminish, the idea that the marathon NBA regular season doesn't start until Christmas, or that teams have to get through it to reach the "real season" of the playoffs. The NBA Cup helps with that.

articles.title: What the Golden State Valkyries must do to win Game 7 of the WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Here are three numbers the Valkyries need to flip in order to bring home their first championship.
articles.body:
ATLANTA – "We don't want to have to come back to Ballhalla."

It was part of a longer answer Kiah Stokes gave to reporters during Wednesday's practice availability. Stokes, and the Golden State Valkyries at large, obviously love their home crowd. It's one of, if not the most electric home court advantage in the WNBA. But going back would signal a Game 6 loss; within that lens, why play in front of that crowd again if you could handle business beforehand?

Ultimately, the Valkyries weren't able to get it done. Save any bail you want to shoot for the earlier-than-expected 12:30 ET tip-off time — nobody on the Golden State side wants it, nor will they use it as an excuse.

A barrage of 3-pointers (6-of-8 in the opening frame), timely drives, and stellar defense sparked a 32-15 first quarter lead for the Atlanta Dream, one they ultimately never relinquished. The Dream were able to notch an impressive 80-69 victory to tie the series, setting up the two most exciting words in sports: Game 7 .

Here are three numbers that popped in the Dream's Game 6 win, numbers the Valkyries need to flip in order to bring home their first championship.

All stats come courtesy of WNBA.com or Second Spectrum/Genius IQ unless otherwise noted.

46% — rate of help defenders shown on Atlanta's drives

The Valkyries' historic defense is headlined by elite defenders — they certainly have those in Gabby Williams, Veronica Burton, and Kiah Stokes, for starters — but their talents are accentuated by the strong help principles around them.

It's hard enough to beat Burton or Williams off the bounce; having to deal with a thicket of arms if you do beat them has to be incredibly annoying. If you make it through that, you also have to deal with Stokes at the rim.

Teams simply don't have fun driving against the Valkyries. Only the Washington Mystics (0.9 PPP) allowed a lower per-possession mark than the Valkyries (0.91 PPP) during the regular season. In terms of having help defenders present on drives, only the Minnesota Lynx (78.4%) and Portland Fire (73.3%) had them available at a higher rate than the Valkyries (72.7%).

It's what made Game 6 such an impressive showing for the Dream offense, and such a weird one to absorb from the Valkyries side. A 46% clip wasn't just the lowest of the series; it was their second-lowest mark in a game all season.

The Dream being able to get out in transition, particularly in the first half, helps explain some of the lack of, well, help. It's hard to build a shell when you're retreating and trying to claim a matchup. Beyond that, the Dream did a great job of mixing their spacing alignments initially — sometimes it was a classic 5-out look, other times they'd start with a "flat" look with the corners filled, plus someone lurking in the dunker spot — and relocating during action to occupy help defenders.

Go back through the Dream's offensive possessions, and you'll see plenty of trips where a player may start in the dunker spot, but they'd backtrack to the corner during a drive. The Dream love "looping" a player from the corner to the wing behind a pick-and-roll, something Angel Reese briefly mentioned during Wednesday's media availability.

Regardless, the Valkyries will need to be more diligent setting up their shell defensively to make life more difficult for Atlanta's offense. The screws tightened after the first quarter, but they're going to need (close to) a full 40 minutes in Game 7.

71.4% — Angel Reese's field goal percentage on shots contested by Kiah Stokes

Reese dusted Stokes midway through the first quarter, attacking her top foot and immediately getting to the basket.

It happened again late in the third, with Reese jabbing to her right before beating Stokes with another lefty drive.

Early in the fourth, it was Reese attacking off a handoff before delivering a bump to Stokes, pivoting, then finishing over her.

It was the most confident and (consistently) aggressive we've seen Reese be against the matchup all series long.

After converting just six of her 25 attempts (24% FG) contested by Stokes through the first five games of the series, Reese went 5-of-7 (71.4%) on those looks in Game 6.

One of the more fascinating stories of the Finals — heck, of the postseason — has been the defensive work of Stokes. As mentioned in this space , she's been on a historic run of interior defense, stifling multiple All-Star bigs to the point where a Finals MVP candidacy was (and probably still is, depending on how Game 7 goes) a very real thing.

She's been a menace to Reese in this series, shutting down post-ups and corralling drives. Contesting shots at a high level, sending others out of bounds — with either hand.

Stokes just didn't have it today, which led to head coach Natalie Nakase limiting her minutes (series-low 20) in favor of former Dream forward Laeticia Amihere, a callback to the first half of Game 1.

"Yeah, I just think her legs weren't moving as well as [Laeticia Amihere's], so that was the decision that we made," Nakase told reporters after Game 6.

The big question now is if Reese has truly flipped things in the matchup, or if she simply (and finally) got the best of Stokes today. The Valkyries have to hope it's the latter.

16.7%: How much Gabby Williams underperformed her expected shot efficiency in the half-court

Second Spectrum has a shot quality metric that factors in shot type, shot distance, the level of shot contest being given by a defender and more. Based on that metric, Williams was expected to have an effective field goal percentage of 50%. Instead, she logged a 33.3% — an "underperformance" of nearly 17 percentage points.

Williams has shot very poorly for most of this series; at the end of the day, 35.3% on 2s and 22.7% on 3s isn't what you want from your top scoring option. But it's hard to say she's played poorly; this hasn't been a high-turnover experience (she has four in her last three games), she's gotten to the spots and shots she's wanted, and she's largely been great defensively.

Among the few silver linings for the Valkyries in Game 6 was Williams finding some semblance of a rhythm in the second half, particularly the fourth quarter.

Williams got especially busy on drives, cycling through defenders — Jordin Canada, Naz Hillmon, DeWanna Bonner and Howard — for buckets, free throws, or both. She splashed home a corner 3 while the Valkyries were attempting to make a furious comeback.

It was nice to see her look more like herself, ultimately finishing with a game-high 26 points (15 in the 4th).

It's a very "no, duh" thing to say, but the Valkyries have to hope that the late shot-making (and foul-drawing) from Williams is able to carry over into Game 7. A true bounceback from her could be enough to put the Valkyries over the top; at the very least, it should bring them much closer to where they want to be offensively.

articles.title: Houston Comets Reveal New Logo in Photos, Videos Ahead of WNBA Return for 2027 Season
articles.summary: The new logo of the Houston Comets has been unveiled.
articles.body:
The new logo of the Houston Comets has been unveiled.

As the Comets prepare to return to the WNBA for the 2027 season, they showcased their updated logo in a series of social media posts on Thursday.

The team was initially part of the WNBA from 1997 through 2008.

In March, the Connecticut Sun were sold to the Fertitta family with plans to relocate to Houston and be renamed as the Comets following the 2026 season.

The new logo shares a similar color scheme as Houston's original logo, although the team couldn't revive the old design as a primary logo due to WNBA rules (h/t USA Today's Danielle Lerner ).

For the new primary logo, there are four stars included in the letter "H" to represent the team's four WNBA championships. There's also a large white star that pays tribute to Texas' nickname, the Lone Star State.

Comets senior creative director Jose Lopez discussed the similarities between the new and old logos.

"The logos, they're a memory," Lopez said, per Lerner. "They're one of the championships that you went to with your family. If you're watching television or listening to the radio and you hear 'Houston Comets,' all those memories come back, right? So when you see these, when you see this color scheme, I think that people will really gravitate to it."

The Comets won championships in each of their first four years with the WNBA, boasting stars including Cynthia Cooper, Sheryl Swoopes and Tina Thompson.

Houston made another WNBA Finals appearance in 2005, but couldn't emerge victorious before missing the playoffs in two of the next three seasons. The WNBA eventually assumed ownership of the Comets in 2008 before the organization was disbanded .

Now, the team is back to host games at Toyota Center starting next season.

articles.title: Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic were not immediate friends, but the Lakers duo eventually developed the NBA’s best basketball chemistry
articles.summary: Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic hardly spoke after the Lakers traded for Doncic in February 2025.
articles.body: Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic hardly spoke after the Lakers traded for Doncic in February 2025. Reaves told the California Post in an interview published Thursday that the two passed each other in the locker room without a word. The silence is long gone. Doncic leads the NBA at 36.0 points per game, Reaves is 16th at 24.4, and together they average 60.4, the most of any duo in the league. Reaves signed a four-year, $180 million deal in July, and Doncic has said he hopes to retire a Laker.How did Austin Reaves and Luka Doncic go from silent teammates to friends?Austin Reaves did not think he and Luka Doncic would ever be friends. He meant it. In an exclusive interview with the California Post, Reaves said the two walked past each other in the locker room for a while with nothing to say. He had no idea how to talk to a superstar who had just arrived against his wishes. His first thought was blunt: “What is this guy going to be like?”Doncic had his own struggle. He had led the Mavericks to the Finals and finished third in MVP voting in 2023-24. Then Dallas traded him. He had wanted to spend his whole career there, and he arrived in Los Angeles feeling betrayed. He kept to himself.Doncic told the paper that joining a new team makes it hard for him to speak, so he stuck with a few people he already knew. The shift came at the next training camp, when he and Reaves got close. Teasing followed. Doncic joked that Reaves wanted to be his friend and he was not allowing it. Reaves fired back that he had more dunks.A summer away helped. Doncic’s hurt turned into determination, and he began to see himself as the face of a 17-time champion franchise. Once he fully bought in, Reaves got to see who he really was.Why is the Reaves and Doncic duo the NBA’s top scoring pair?The numbers back up the jokes. Doncic leads the league at 36.0 points per game and adds 8.3 assists and 6.8 rebounds. He shoots 48.4 percent from the field and 39.6 percent from three.The $180 million guard sits 16th in scoring at 24.4 points. Reaves also averages 5.4 assists and 3.4 rebounds while hitting 56.9 percent of his shots and 48.1 percent from deep. He is the more efficient shooter on both marks, which says a lot about how the two share the floor.Together they produce 60.4 points a game. Steph Curry and Yaxel Lendeborg are second at 51.4, nine points back.Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O’Neal peaked at a combined 57.5 in 2001-02, during the Lakers’ run of three straight titles. Doncic and Reaves are above that mark. The sample is small this early in the season, but the gap to second place is wide.What do Reaves and Doncic have in common off the court?Once Doncic settled in, the two found they had plenty in common. Reaves said they share a sense of humor and act alike. Both are understated, and both would rather spend time with loved ones than work the LA scene. Golf is how they unwind. In July, Reaves said Doncic sends him videos of his swing and asks how to improve. Reaves tells him he is no coach.The bonding went on all summer. Doncic hosted several teammates in Slovenia for golf, group activities and basketball, and he and Reaves led opposing teams in a rowing contest. Kevon Looney later said time like that lets teammates learn each other’s personalities before camp starts.The ribbing is still going. Late in September, Reaves lost his train of thought in a media session because Doncic was hitting long shots on the practice floor. Reaves said Doncic had made five half-court shots in about 30 seconds, then joked that he hated him.How did the two guards handle last season’s injuries?The bond showed on the court too. LeBron James missed the start of last season with sciatica, and Doncic and Reaves led the Lakers to a 15-4 start. When James sat out three games in March with several ailments, they beat the Pacers, Knicks and Timberwolves and sparked a 15-2 run.April 2 brought bad luck for both. Each got hurt against the Thunder, and the Lakers’ playoff hopes took a hit. Doncic strained a hamstring and missed the whole postseason. Reaves strained an oblique and sat out the first four games of the first-round series against the Rockets.Reaves had a big decision looming as well. He planned to turn down his $14.9 million player option and hit free agency, hoping to stay with the Lakers. In season, he said, the two are around each other about 95 percent of the time, with an off day every week or two. They travel together and know what the other is going through. Having each other around, he said, helped both of them.Does Doncic want to stay with the Lakers long term?Everything points that way. Last summer Doncic told Lakers brass two things mattered to him: a franchise center, and Reaves staying put. James left for the 76ers in July, and the team’s top priority was keeping its centerpiece happy. The Lakers signed Reaves to the four-year, $180 million deal that month. It is the richest contract in NBA history for an undrafted player.Asked if he wants to retire as a Laker, Doncic told the Post, “Hopefully, yeah.”Reaves was just as open in Las Vegas after the signing. He called Doncic one of his best friends on the planet and said they talk almost every day.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
